goal: Ship the first functional multi-agent orchestration layer on top of the 0.2.0 terminal and Git-worktree foundation.
release_principles: Terminal, agent, task, worktree, and orchestrator are separate entities.
The Electron main process remains authoritative for processes, Git, persistence, and orchestration lifecycle.
Agents use structured provider events instead of terminal text as their lifecycle protocol.
One writable Git worktree may be assigned to at most one agent at a time.
Automatic merge and branch deletion remain disabled by default.

tasks.title: Define the 0.3.0 orchestration scope and model
acceptance_criteria: Project workspace, orchestrator, agent, task, runtime, terminal, and Git workspace boundaries are documented.
Lifecycle states, event names, user limits, persistence, security, and deferred integration behavior are explicit.
The design preserves the shipped 0.2.0 terminal and worktree safety contracts.

tasks.title: Add orchestration models, persistence, events, and prompt contracts
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrations, agents, and dependency-aware tasks have validated explicit state.
State is persisted atomically and interrupted runs recover without implying that processes survived restart.
Structured orchestrator and worker instructions are generated consistently without logging their content.

tasks.title: Implement the provider abstraction and Codex App Server adapter
acceptance_criteria: The orchestration layer depends on a provider contract rather than terminal input or Codex-specific lifecycle assumptions.
The Codex provider uses the local App Server JSON-RPC thread, turn, item, and interrupt lifecycle.
Provider process trees are disposed on stop and application shutdown without logging prompts or responses.

tasks.title: Implement safe agent worktree provisioning and scheduling
acceptance_criteria: The orchestrator creates one stable agent, terminal definition, branch, and isolated worktree per implementation task.
Ready tasks start only after dependencies complete and active agents never exceed maxAgents.
Partial failures preserve pre-existing Git work and never share a writable worktree.

tasks.title: Expose narrow orchestration IPC and lifecycle events
acceptance_criteria: The renderer can start, list, observe, and stop orchestration through validated intent-specific APIs.
The project path is resolved from a current main-process workspace rather than accepted from the renderer.
UI events expose structured state without terminal output, prompts, arbitrary commands, or filesystem authority.

tasks.title: Add the minimal orchestration interface
acceptance_criteria: The user can enter a goal, select maxAgents, start and stop a run, and inspect orchestrator, task, and agent status.
An agent entry can focus its associated terminal/worktree pane.
The existing dynamic terminal and Git workspace interface remains usable.

tasks.title: Validate and document the 0.3.0 orchestration foundation
acceptance_criteria: Automated tests cover plan validation, dependency scheduling, limits, provider events, IPC validation, persistence, stop, and cleanup.
Linting, formatting, unit tests, and the production build pass.
README and architecture documentation describe the new workflow, safety boundaries, privacy, and known limitations.

tasks.title: Add project workspace navigation and workspace-scoped terminals
acceptance_criteria: A persistent Workspaces sidebar adds and selects project folders independently from terminals.
New terminals inherit and start in the active project workspace without accepting renderer-provided paths.
Orchestration targets the active project workspace and agent terminals remain associated with it.
Parallel worktree provisioning serializes preview and creation per repository without reducing agent execution concurrency.
